metadata.title: Teachers’ Frequency of ICT Use in Providing Sustainable Opportunity to Learn: Mediation Analysis Using aReading Database

survey_design.weight_fields_interpretation: The study uses PISA 2018 teacher questionnaire data for three regions (Hong Kong, Macau, Chinese Taipei) and estimates a multilevel mediation model with teachers nested in schools and regions. The manuscript does not report applying PISA sampling weights or any specific weight variable (e.g., W_FSTUWT/TOTWGT) and does not mention replicate-weight procedures (e.g., BRR/jackknife), so weight usage cannot be confirmed. Because the analysis is conducted in lavaan (structural equation modeling) and focuses on mediation paths rather than achievement PVs, the authors’ weighting strategy is not documented; analysts should consult the PISA 2018 teacher questionnaire documentation to apply the appropriate complex-survey weights if population-representative estimates are required. The analytic sample is restricted to reading teachers in the specified regions and further processed via EM-based missing-data imputation and Z-score standardization before modeling.

data.handling_not_reported_explanation: Plausible values are not applicable because the dependent variables are derived teacher-reported questionnaire constructs (ICT use frequency, opportunities to learn in reading comprehension, teacher self-efficacy, and adaptive instruction), not PISA cognitive achievement scores that are typically represented via PVs. Missing data handling is described (EM imputation), so the missing-data strategy is not a reporting gap; however, the paper does not document any PV-related procedures because PVs are not part of this teacher-questionnaire mediation framework.

sample_details.sample_filtering_criteria: Used PISA 2018 teacher questionnaire data and extracted a sample of reading teachers from three regions: Hong Kong, Macau, and Chinese Taipei. The paper reports a total of 10,796 teachers from 389 schools, and the mediation model is estimated separately for novice (≤5 years) and experienced (>5 years) teachers. Missing values in the analytic variables were imputed using expectation maximization (EM) prior to modeling, and all variables were standardized using Z-scores. No additional task-level or item-level filtering is described beyond restricting to reading teachers and the three specified regions.

main_findings.dataset_used: PISA 2018 Teacher Questionnaire (Reading teachers; Hong Kong, Macau, Chinese Taipei)
main_findings.target_variable: Frequency of providing opportunities to learn in reading comprehension (TCOTLCOMP)
main_findings.standardized_conclusion: Using PISA 2018 teacher questionnaire data for reading teachers in Hong Kong, Macau, and Chinese Taipei, the study leveraged ICT use frequency in classrooms and teaching experience (novice/experienced) to predict the frequency of providing opportunities to learn in reading comprehension, finding that higher teacher ICT use was positively associated with OTL for both novice and experienced teachers across all three regions (direct effects c’ β≈0.22–0.36; total effects c β≈0.34–0.47). This indicates that strengthening teachers’ regular ICT integration in reading instruction may increase the frequency of classroom practices that support students’ reading opportunities to learn, though the study is correlational/mediation-based and relies on self-reported teacher measures.

main_findings.dataset_used: PISA 2018 Teacher Questionnaire (Reading teachers; Hong Kong, Macau, Chinese Taipei)
main_findings.target_variable: Mediation of ICT use on opportunities to learn via teacher self-efficacy (SEFFINS → TCOTLCOMP)
main_findings.standardized_conclusion: Using PISA 2018 teacher questionnaire data for reading teachers in Hong Kong, Macau, and Chinese Taipei, the study leveraged ICT use frequency in classrooms and teacher self-efficacy in instruction to predict opportunities to learn in reading comprehension through a mediation pathway, finding that self-efficacy significantly mediated the ICT use–OTL relationship in Chinese Taipei and Macau for both novice and experienced teachers, but not for novice teachers in Hong Kong. This indicates that ICT professional support should be paired with interventions that build teachers’ instructional self-efficacy to translate technology use into more frequent reading opportunities to learn, while recognizing that this mechanism may vary by region and teacher experience.

main_findings.dataset_used: PISA 2018 Teacher Questionnaire (Reading teachers; Hong Kong, Macau, Chinese Taipei)
main_findings.target_variable: Mediation of ICT use on opportunities to learn via teacher adaptive instruction (ADAPTINSTR → TCOTLCOMP)
main_findings.performance_metrics: Mediation paths (a2b2): Chinese Taipei—Novice β=0.1000 (B=0.1000, 95% CI [0.0893, 0.1110]); Experienced β=0.1032 (B=0.1028, 95% CI [0.0912, 0.1143]). Hong Kong—Novice β=0.0733 (B=0.0808, 95% CI [0.0399, 0.1216]); Experienced β=0.0714 (B=0.0708, 95% CI [0.0609, 0.0808]). Macau—Novice β=0.0689 (B=0.0696, 95% CI [0.0586, 0.0806]); Experienced β=0.0654 (B=0.0658, 95% CI [0.0535, 0.0782]). Proportion mediated (overall): 23.00%–40.20% (medium-to-large), with less evident mediation for novice than experienced teachers.
main_findings.standardized_conclusion: Using PISA 2018 teacher questionnaire data for reading teachers in Hong Kong, Macau, and Chinese Taipei, the study leveraged ICT use frequency in classrooms and teacher adaptive instruction to predict opportunities to learn in reading comprehension through a mediation pathway, finding that adaptive instruction significantly mediated the ICT use–OTL relationship across regions and teacher experience groups and showed larger standardized coefficients than self-efficacy. This indicates that policy and school-level ICT initiatives should emphasize pedagogical adaptation skills (tailoring instruction, providing individual help, and adjusting lesson structure) so that technology use results in more frequent, responsive reading opportunities to learn.

data.outcome_summary: This study uses PISA 2018 teacher questionnaire data from reading teachers in Hong Kong (HKG), Macau (MAC), and Chinese Taipei (TWN) to test a multilevel mediation model linking teachers’ ICT use frequency to opportunities to learn (OTL) in reading comprehension. The analysis is multilevel (teachers nested in schools/regions) and estimates mediation via two parallel mediators: teacher self-efficacy in instruction (SEFFINS) and teacher adaptive instruction (ADAPTINSTR). Missing data were imputed using expectation maximization (EM), and variables were standardized with Z-scores; the paper does not report any machine-learning model or PV-based achievement metrics. Results show positive total and direct effects of ICT use on OTL across regions and both novice and experienced teachers (direct effects β≈0.22–0.36; total effects β≈0.34–0.47). Mediation is significant for adaptive instruction across groups, while self-efficacy mediation fails for novice teachers in Hong Kong. Because measures are self-reported and the design is correlational/mediation-based, causal claims about ICT improving OTL should be interpreted cautiously.
